text:
Alex: Heads-up: after pushing driver 535.86 + kernel 6.4 on the canary fleet at 02:10 UTC we got a spike in Xid 13/31/43 across 5 nodes. Alert: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abcd/gpu-xid-dashboard
Priya: Saw same. first Xid 13 around 02:14 on gpu-canary-03. dmesg shows "NVRM: Xid (13)" and repeated "NCCL Watchdog detected stale completion" entries.
Marco: Rolling back canary now? Which component likely culprit: driver, kernel, or NCCL binary update? We upgraded NCCL to 2.14.3 in the same batch.
Jen: Oncall checking node logs. `dmesg | tail -n 200` shows repeated GPU resets and `nvidia-persistenced` restarting.
SREBot: Incident created: INC-2025-0789. PagerDuty alerted to infra-oncall.
Priya: Quick inventory: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,name,driver_version,pstate --format=csv` shows driver 535.86, kernel 6.4.8, CUDA 12.2, NCCL 2.14.3 on canary nodes.
Alex: Metric spike: `increase(nvidia_gpu_xid_errors_total[5m])` jumped to 32 on the canary cluster.
Marco: I reproduced on a dev-box with identical stack: running a long-lived attention-batch job causes nv-hostengine watchdog to fire after ~20s.
Jen: Recommendation: pause rollout to prod, scale down GPU job replicas in canary to 0, and roll back driver to 535.54 (last known-good).
Priya: Opening rollback patch for node image: `image: redwood-gpu:2025-03-12-driver-535.54` and kicking off automated redeploy now.
Alex: Also adding a temporary Prometheus alert rule: `expr: increase(nvidia_gpu_xid_errors_total[10m]) > 10` for 1m -> severity=critical.
Marco: Runbook pointer: https://runbooks.redwood.example/gpu-upgrades. Steps B & C cover Xid handling and NCCL watchdog timeouts; follow the diagnostics checklist.
Jen: While rolling back, collect NVML dumps: `sudo python /opt/tools/gpu_dump.py --out /tmp/gpu-dump.gz` and attach to the incident ticket. Also grab `journalctl -k | grep -i nvrm` and kube container restart counts.
Priya: Rollback started at 02:37 UTC. Daemonset reimage applied to canary nodes; draining and cordoning nodes sequentially.
Alex: Post-rollback update: Xid rate dropping to baseline. gpu-canary-03 shows no new Xid for ~20m after rollback.
Marco: Action items: 1) Lock driver version across fleets until compatibility matrix updated. 2) Add canary telemetry for NCCL watchdog logs + nv-hostengine traces. 3) Run 24h soak tests under stress harness before next driver/kernel bump.
Jen: We'll also add an alert for `node_exporter:gpu_watchdog_count` and correlate with `kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total` to catch early regressions.
Priya: I'll draft a postmortem with timeline + reproducer and assign to Marco for root cause analysis.
Alex: Thanks. If anyone has repro scripts or instrumented nvml captures that trigger this faster, drop them into the incident thread.
Ravi: FYI hardware confirms no faulty cards found; likely a software regression in driver/NCCL/kernel combination.
Priya: Marking incident mitigated at 03:12 UTC — monitoring will stay on high alert for next 24h.
Jen: 👍 :thumbsup:
